samples.summary: The new cross-site check is placed in a layer the attack navigation never reaches: `CliLoginConfirmMiddleware` runs before the guard and terminates every unconfirmed `?mode=cli` navigation itself, so `assertCliStartNotCrossSite` only ever sees the same-origin confirmation click.
samples.evidence: packages/backend/src/auth/cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:113 answers an unconfirmed `?mode=cli` request with `res.status(200).send(renderConfirmPage(...))` and never calls `next()`, so the guard is not reached for that request at all. packages/backend/src/auth/auth.module.ts:45-49 registers that middleware on `GET auth/github`, and Nest middleware always runs ahead of guards (the comment at auth.module.ts:41-43 states this explicitly). The only requests that do reach `canActivate` with a usable port are those carrying a `confirm=` secret matching the httpOnly cookie (middleware:91-103) — i.e. the click on the backend-served confirmation page, whose `Sec-Fetch-Site` is `same-origin` by construction and therefore always in `ALLOWED_FETCH_SITES`. A hostile page's cross-site navigation gets the confirmation page (and a fresh confirm cookie) exactly as before; nothing about it is refused. If the intent is to refuse a cross-site-initiated CLI start, the check has to run in the middleware (before the confirm page is served), not in the guard behind it.

samples.summary: The check keys off `req.query.mode === 'cli'` alone, contradicting the middleware's documented fall-through for a `mode=cli` request with an unusable `port`, which is supposed to continue as an ordinary browser login (a flow the diff itself argues is legitimately cross-site).
samples.evidence: packages/backend/src/auth/cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:78-82: `if (port === undefined) { // Not a usable CLI request. The guard ignores it too, so it falls through to an ordinary browser login rather than 404-ing here. return next(); }`. After this change the guard no longer ignores it: `const isCliStart = req.query?.mode === 'cli'; if (isCliStart) this.assertCliStartNotCrossSite(req);` runs before `parseCliPort`, so `/auth/github?mode=cli&port=notanumber` navigated in from another site now 400s where the same navigation without `mode=cli` is deliberately served (the guard's own doc comment says a browser login is routinely cross-site). Gating the new check on `port !== undefined && req.__cliConfirmed` — the same condition the CLI branch uses — would keep the two modules' contracts aligned.

samples.summary: The image fetcher's new operator-facing warning writes to stderr unconditionally because neither CLI call site supplies the new `warn` seam, so `--quiet` no longer gates all non-essential notices.
samples.evidence: `createImageFetcher` gained a `warn` option defaulting to `defaultWarn` (packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts, `process.stderr.write('[wafflebase] …')`), but the two production call sites — packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:281 and packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:224 — pass only `serverBase`, so the proxy pin-dropped notice is emitted even under `--quiet`, which docs/design/cli.md documents as gating progress/notice output (the result body and error envelope being the deliberate exceptions). Threading `opts.quiet` into `warn` at both call sites would restore that.

verdict.reason: The layering the reviewer describes is real (middleware terminates unconfirmed ?mode=cli at cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:113; registered on GET auth/github at auth.module.ts:45-49; no global prefix in main.ts:31), but it does not amount to a blast-radius defect. The operation the check protects — minting the CLI state token for an attacker-chosen loopback port — is already guarded by `req.__cliConfirmed` (github-auth.guard.ts:116), set only by the single-use confirm secret matched against the httpOnly cookie (middleware.ts:91-104). The cross-site navigation therefore reaches only an inert confirmation page, not any protected operation, so nothing bypasses the guard and no caller is left broken (the sole ?mode=cli producer, packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:262, always sends a port and is opened by the OS opener; the browser login link, frontend/src/components/login-form.tsx:63, never sets mode=cli). What is left of the finding — that the new check is redundant/placed in the wrong layer, and its comments overstate its effect — is a security-design and diff-internal-logic judgement explicitly outside this lens, and at most minor here (stale comment), not blocking.
